value: Responding to widespread anxieties and calls for regulation concerning large language models like ChatGPT and hypothetical "foom" scenarios, this article argues against prematurely halting AI progress. It contends that historical patterns suggest a gradual, multi-century transition to an AI-dominated economy, not a sudden, uncontrolled explosion. While acknowledging control challenges inherent in large organizations, the author asserts these are currently manageable and future AI control will similarly be addressed as concrete problems emerge, best learned through experience rather than speculative foresight. The article dismisses the "foom" scenario as highly improbable and warns that preemptive regulation, historically, has often stopped rather than merely slowed beneficial technological advancement, making it an ill-advised approach to a future whose specific challenges are not yet clear.
